title: The House of Avtinas
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: They are mentioned in Mishnah Shekalim, beginning of chapter 5, as having been in charge of making the incense in the Temple. They had a special chamber for making the incense, called the Chamber of the House of Avtinas, as in Yoma 1:5, and there in the Gemara, 19a. In Yoma 3:11, those of the House of Avtinas did not want to teach about making the incense. In the Gemara there, 38a, the sages sent and brought other craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt, but the new ones did not know how to make the smoke rise as they did, and the sages had to double the wage of the House of Avtinas. When they asked them why they refused to teach, they answered: “Those of our father’s house knew that this House is destined to be destroyed, and perhaps an unworthy person would learn it and go and serve idolatry with it.” For this they are mentioned favorably: a perfumed bride never went out of their houses, and when they married a woman from elsewhere they stipulated with her that she would not perfume herself, etc.

notes.text: לשבת בית אבטינוס is understood as the Chamber of the House of Avtinas. Their smoke-making skill, double wage and refusal to perfume brides remain separate supplied claims, without new family identity binding.

The consulted Yoma 38a incense account directly gives the Alexandrian craftsmen’s different smoke, the doubled wages, the reason for withholding instruction and the condition about perfume. These are the Avtinas episode; they are not combined with the adjacent Garmu bread-making account.
